name: Reflexion
input:
Write a function is_valid_parens(s) that returns True when every bracket in s — (), [] and {} — is closed in the right order, and False otherwise.

Tests:
assert is_valid_parens('()[]{}')
assert is_valid_parens('{[()]}')
assert not is_valid_parens('(]')
assert not is_valid_parens('([)]')
assert not is_valid_parens('((')
assert is_valid_parens('')
assert is_valid_parens('a(b)c')

system.name: Reflexion
system.description: The actor writes a solution; the evaluator runs the tests on it. When they fail, the self-reflection agent studies the attempt and the failures and writes a lesson into the episodic memory. The actor reads every lesson before its next trial, so each attempt learns from the last — no weights change, only words.

tools.description: Run shell commands in the sandbox
Read and write files in the sandbox

data.name: User
data.role: Gives the task and its tests

harness.instructions: Solve the task: write the function to /work/solution.py with edit_file. Before you start, read the lessons from your earlier trials in your context and do not repeat those mistakes. Reply with the code.

Write the task's tests to /work/test_solution.py as pytest tests (import from solution), run them with run_tests (command: python -m pytest -q), and report. If every test passes, reply PASS and the code. Otherwise reply FAIL with each failing test and its error.

data.name: Self-reflection
data.role: Turns a failure into a lesson

harness.instructions: You see a failed attempt and why it failed. Write one or two sentences of advice to your future self: what went wrong, and what to do differently. Be specific to this task. Reply with the lesson only.

fn.code:
// a pass leaves the trial; a failure goes to self-reflection
return String(input.text ?? input).includes('PASS') ? { done: input } : { reflect: input };

after_turn.code: List new durable facts from this turn (preferences, decisions, open items), one per line.
